summary.title: Lessons from Keith Rabois Essay 5: How to Become a Magnet for Talent and Assess Talent
summary.one_liner: Early-stage startup hiring advice: tell your story publicly, source candidates from your network and from later-stage companies, assess risk appetite and generalist learning ability, and move fast on offers.
takeaways: Your first 10 hires set the bar for later hires, so prioritize hiring quality early and hire people who can run with ambiguous roles.
Build a public story (a 'trailer') and announce financing with hiring in mind, since this helps attract candidates over time.
Scale interview effort with fit and enthusiasm: cold outreach, 30-min phone screen, 1-hr coffee, then 4-hr on-site, and consider a paid 3-day to 2-week trial.
Look for risk takers, generalists, and self-directed learners rather than candidates on a traditional career ladder.
Move quickly on offers, and consider a dedicated recruiter once you are hiring 3-4 roles at a time.
summary.summary: This essay by Keith Rabois gives advice for early-stage founders on hiring and recruiting talent. It covers how to publicly tell your startup's story, how to source candidates from your network and from later-stage companies on LinkedIn, and how to structure an interview pipeline with increasing time investment. It also describes how to assess candidates for risk appetite, generalist ability, growth mindset, and tenacity, and ends with advice on closing offers and when to hire a recruiter. The approach is anecdotal, drawing on examples such as Elon Musk's Tesla plan, Austen Allred's Lambda School tweets, and specific founder mistakes.
